chapter_name: Mask Making and Mixed Material Crafts
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the rich cultural tradition of masks and learn to design character faces using papier-mâché and mixed materials!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Masks are a powerful form of expression. In traditional Indian arts (like Chhau dance or Ramlila), masks are used to represent gods, demons, animals, and mythological characters, completely hiding the actor's real identity.

A popular method for mask making. It involves pasting strips of newspaper coated with a glue mixture (like maida paste or fevicol) over a mold (like a balloon). When it dries, it becomes a hard, paintable shell.
The shape of the eyes, eyebrows, and mouth on a mask determines its character. Angled eyebrows create anger, wide eyes show surprise, and curved lines show joy.
A mask isn't just painted. Artists use 'mixed materials' like wool for hair, beads for jewelry, feathers, sequences, and mirrors to make the craft look rich and theatrical.
Mask making bridges drawing (designing the face) and sculpture (building the 3D form), making it an excellent exercise in understanding facial contours.

fun_activity.title: 🎈 The Balloon Mask
fun_activity.instructions: Inflate a balloon. Mix water and glue. Dip strips of newspaper into the glue and cover half the balloon with 4-5 layers. Let it dry completely overnight. Pop the balloon, and you have a hard, hollow face shape ready to be painted and decorated as a mask!

exam_tips: 📌 Be ready to name Indian classical or folk dances that use masks (e.g., Chhau dance, Kathakali uses mask-like heavy makeup).
📌 Explain the process of Papier-mâché clearly: layering paper strips with an adhesive binder until hard.
📌 Embellishments (like beads, wool, shells) are what give a craft its finished, professional look.
quick_recap: ⭐ Masks have been used in human rituals and theatre for thousands of years.
⭐ Papier-mâché is an eco-friendly craft as it upcycles waste newspaper.
⭐ Exaggerated features (very large eyes, big teeth) are common in masks so they can be seen clearly from a distance on a stage.
